notes: Prices in USD cents per 1,000,000 tokens (provider list prices). See README.md for the update process and the field reference. Per-model metadata: display_name (UI label), provider (the model's AUTHOR, e.g. anthropic), hoster (who serves the API we call, e.g. google-vertex), location (most specific hosting region: global | europe | germany | baden-wuerttemberg; each level implies the broader ones, so baden-wuerttemberg is also germany- and europe-hosted). location describes the DEFAULT SaaS routing; compliance-authoritative residency stays with the app's routing code, which a deployment can repoint. Anthropic entries split plain input (input_cents_per_mtok = base 1x) from cache writes (cache_write_cents_per_mtok = 5m cache-write rate); requires app >= cache-write-bucket release. tier_threshold_tokens overrides the default 200k tier boundary; tier_boundary_inclusive=true means >= instead of >. Field names *_above_200k are legacy labels: the real boundary is tier_threshold_tokens when set.

flux-2-klein-4b.manual_only_reason: Black Forest Labs FLUX.2; no BFL scraper in repo. BFL prices per MEGAPIXEL, not per image, and its docs publish only a 'from' floor plus an interactive calculator — so these per-size values are derived by hand and must be maintained that way.
flux-2-klein-4b.notes: ADDED 2026-09-07 — the row was missing entirely while the model was live in the app's IMAGE_MODELS, so every FLUX generation billed 0 (computeImageCost returns 0 + a console.warn for an unknown model). BFL's model, confirmed exactly against its own calculator: price = base + increment x (total MP - 1), with base $0.014 at 1 MP and increment $0.001/MP (docs example '2MP = $0.014 + $0.001 = $0.015' and calculator 3 MP = $0.016 both fit). 1024x1024 is 1.0 MP = $0.014; 1024x1536 and 1536x1024 are 1.5 MP = $0.0145. FRACTIONAL MP CHARGED PRO RATA: BFL publishes the increment as a RATE ('$0.002/MP' on the klein-9b card), which reads as continuous, so the half-megapixel is charged as half. BFL's calculator only offers whole MP (1/2/3/4) — that is a UI limit, not billing policy; do not re-derive these from it. FLUX has no quality tiers (qualities: null), so the app always sends quality 'auto' (generate.ts:304 via imageModelHasQualityTiers) and pricing.ts reads only pricing.auto[size]. ALL FOUR QUALITY KEYS ARE MANDATORY ANYWAY — QualitySizeImageEntry in pricing-registry.ts declares low/medium/high/auto WITHOUT .optional(), so an 'auto'-only row fails schema validation. That failure is catastrophic, not local: loadFromUpstream parses the whole document in one call, so one bad image row leaves the ENTIRE pricing cache empty and every model in the file bills 0 — and at boot there is no previous cache to fall back on, so all 10-minute retries fail identically. The union error is also misleading (it reports 'Expected one of flat' and 'cents_per_image: Required', sending the reader toward the wrong fix). An 'auto'-only draft of these five rows was written and reverted on 2026-09-07 for exactly this reason. Do NOT prune the duplicates, and do NOT make the schema keys optional either: this file is fetched by already-deployed apps including on-prem installs on older builds, so any shape change must stay backwards-compatible with the oldest running consumer. KNOWN UNDER-BILL: BFL also charges for INPUT megapixels, but the app passes only the output size to computeImageCost, so image EDITS under-bill by the input image's share (~$0.001/MP here).

flux-2-klein-9b.manual_only_reason: Black Forest Labs FLUX.2; no BFL scraper in repo. Per-megapixel pricing derived by hand from BFL's calculator — see notes.
flux-2-klein-9b.notes: ADDED 2026-09-07 — was missing while live in the app, billing 0. Base $0.015 at 1 MP, increment $0.002/MP — confirmed two ways: BFL's calculator (3 MP = $0.019) and BFL's own model card, which prints the rate as '$0.002/MP'. 1024x1024 = 1.0 MP = $0.015; the 1.5 MP sizes = $0.016, charged PRO RATA (the '/MP' rate notation is continuous; the calculator's whole-MP-only input is a UI limit, not billing policy). No quality tiers, so the app always sends 'auto' and pricing.ts reads only pricing.auto[size] — all four quality keys present because QualitySizeImageEntry requires low/medium/high/auto without .optional() — an 'auto'-only row fails validation and, since loadFromUpstream parses the whole document at once, would leave the entire pricing cache empty and bill EVERY model 0. Do not prune the duplicates. Image EDITS under-bill: BFL charges input megapixels too, which the app does not pass to computeImageCost. Note weber.cloud also serves black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein — if klein is ever routed through weber instead of api.eu.bfl.ai, this price no longer applies.

flux-2-pro.notes: ADDED 2026-09-07 — was missing while live in the app, billing 0. Base $0.03 at 1 MP, increment $0.015/MP (BFL calculator: 3 MP = $0.060). 1024x1024 = 1.0 MP = $0.03; the 1.5 MP sizes = $0.0375, charged PRO RATA (BFL prints the increment as a per-MP rate, which is continuous; its calculator's whole-MP-only input is a UI limit). No quality tiers, so the app always sends 'auto' and pricing.ts reads only pricing.auto[size] — all four quality keys present because QualitySizeImageEntry requires low/medium/high/auto without .optional() — an 'auto'-only row fails validation and, since loadFromUpstream parses the whole document at once, would leave the entire pricing cache empty and bill EVERY model 0. Do not prune the duplicates. SEPARATE EDIT RATE NOT REPRESENTABLE: BFL charges $0.045 to EDIT vs $0.03 to generate at 1 MP (a 50% premium), but this schema holds one price per model id and both generate.ts and edit.ts look up the same key — so pro edits bill at the generate rate. This is the largest known gap on any FLUX row.

flux-2-flex.notes: ADDED 2026-09-07 — was missing while live in the app, billing 0. Base $0.05 at 1 MP, increment $0.05/MP (BFL calculator: 3 MP = $0.150) — the steepest per-megapixel scaling of any FLUX model (increment equals the base), so resolution matters most on this row. 1024x1024 = 1.0 MP = $0.05; the 1.5 MP sizes = $0.075, charged PRO RATA. An earlier draft priced these at the 2 MP step ($0.10) on the theory that BFL bills whole megapixels — that was wrong and over-charged this row by 25%; BFL prints the increment as a per-MP RATE, and its calculator's whole-MP-only input is a UI limit rather than billing policy. No quality tiers, so the app always sends 'auto' and pricing.ts reads only pricing.auto[size] — all four quality keys present because QualitySizeImageEntry requires low/medium/high/auto without .optional() — an 'auto'-only row fails validation and, since loadFromUpstream parses the whole document at once, would leave the entire pricing cache empty and bill EVERY model 0. Do not prune the duplicates. Image EDITS under-bill: BFL charges input megapixels too (~$0.05/MP here), which the app does not pass to computeImageCost.
